claim: The project can say what a capture costs in worker time, for the first time.
evidence: A tool now exists that adds up how long each recorded page occupied a capture machine, so the fleet's cost can be stated rather than guessed. It reports 54.11 machine-hours across 5,395 of the 5,396 recordings it found, with a middle value of 27.4 seconds per page. The figure is summed per recording from each recording's own timings, never from elapsed time multiplied by the number of machines. (`fleet:hours`, built by orchestrator on branch `lead/fleet-hours`, commit `10ad2e5`; tracked as issue #21.)
boardClaim: We can say for the first time how much machine time it costs to record a page with a screen reader.
